<laravel-boost-guidelines>
Laravel app using: laravel/fortify v1, laravel/framework v12, laravel/prompts v0, laravel/socialite v5, livewire/flux v2, livewire/livewire v4, laravel/boost v2, laravel/mcp v0, laravel/pail v1, laravel/pint v1, laravel/sail v1, pestphp/pest v4, phpunit/phpunit v12.

Activate relevant skills whenever working in their domain:
- `fluxui-development`: Flux/UI components, forms, inputs, buttons, modals, dropdowns, checkboxes, or Flux mentions.
- `livewire-development`: Livewire components/directives, reactivity, loading states, debugging, or tests.
- `pest-testing`: tests, assertions, datasets, mocks, browser testing, failures, coverage, or verification.
- `tailwindcss-development`: styling, Tailwind, layout, colors, typography, responsive/dark mode, or visual changes.
- `developing-with-fortify`: authentication, registration, password reset, verification, 2FA, profiles, guards, or Fortify.

Follow existing conventions; inspect sibling files when editing or creating files. Use descriptive names, reuse existing components, and keep the existing directory structure. Do not change dependencies without approval. Do not create verification scripts or tinker when tests cover that functionality and prove they work. You must only create documentation files if explicitly requested by the user. Be concise.

Use Boost MCP tools. Use `list-artisan-commands` for Artisan parameters; `get-absolute-url` for project URLs; `tinker` for PHP/Eloquent debugging; `database-query` for read-only database access; `database-schema` before migrations/models; and `browser-logs` for recent browser logs only. Always use `search-docs` before code changes for version-specific Laravel/ecosystem documentation. Use broad topic queries, multiple queries when useful, and do not add package names. Query syntax: word search auto-stems; space means AND; quoted phrases require adjacency; mixed terms combine AND; multiple queries mean ANY.

If frontend changes are not reflected, ask the user to run `npm run build`, `npm run dev`, or `composer run dev`. If Vite manifest errors occur, run `npm run build` or ask the user to run `npm run dev` or `composer run dev`.

Always use curly braces for control structures, including single-line bodies. Use PHP 8 constructor property promotion (`public function __construct(public GitHub $github) { }`). Do not allow empty `__construct()` methods with zero parameters unless the constructor is private. Always declare explicit return types and parameter type hints. Prefer TitleCase Enum keys, PHPDoc blocks over inline comments, and useful array-shape definitions. Never use comments within the code itself unless the logic is exceptionally complex.

Every change must be programmatically tested: write/update a test and run affected tests. Run the minimum tests, using `php artisan test --compact` with a filename or filter. Run `vendor/bin/pint --dirty --format agent` before finalizing. Do not run `vendor/bin/pint --test --format agent`, simply run `vendor/bin/pint --format agent` to fix any formatting issues.

=== Laravel ===
Use `php artisan make:` to create files; pass `--no-interaction` and correct `--options`. Use `php artisan make:class` for generic classes. Use typed Eloquent relationships, prefer models/relationships and `Model::query()` over raw queries, avoid `DB::`, prevent N+1 with eager loading, and use query builder only for complex operations. New models should include useful factories/seeders; ask whether needed and use `list-artisan-commands` to check `php artisan make:model` options. Use API Resources/versioning unless existing API conventions differ. Always create Form Request classes with rules and custom messages; follow sibling array/string rule style. Use built-in auth/authorization. Prefer named routes and `route()`. Queue time-consuming work with `ShouldQueue`. Use environment variables only in config files; never use `env()` directly outside config files; use `config('app.name')`, not `env('APP_NAME')`. Use factories and existing states in tests. Follow existing Faker style. Create feature tests with `php artisan make:test [options] {name}` and unit tests with `--unit`; most tests should be feature tests.

Laravel 12 uses the streamlined structure: middleware are configured in `bootstrap/app.php` via `Application::configure()->withMiddleware()`; `bootstrap/app.php` registers middleware, exceptions, and routing; `bootstrap/providers.php` contains providers; `app\Console\Kernel.php` no longer exists; use `bootstrap/app.php` or `routes/console.php`. Commands in `app/Console/Commands/` are auto-available. When modifying a column, include all previously defined attributes or they will be dropped. Limit eager-loaded records with `$query->latest()->limit(10);`. Prefer a model `casts()` method when consistent with existing models.

=== Flux ===
Flux UI Free includes free components/variants, not Pro. Use `<flux:*>` when available. IMPORTANT: Activate `fluxui-development` when working with Flux UI components.

=== Livewire ===
Use Alpine.js only when client-side interaction requires it; state stays server-side and actions validate/authorize. IMPORTANT: Activate `livewire-development` every time you're working with Livewire-related tasks.

=== Pest ===
This project uses Pest. Create tests: `php artisan make:test --pest {name}`. Run tests: `php artisan test --compact` or filter: `php artisan test --compact --filter=testName`. Do NOT delete tests without approval. CRITICAL: ALWAYS use `search-docs` tool for version-specific Pest documentation and updated code examples. IMPORTANT: Activate `pest-testing` every time you're working with a Pest or testing-related task.

=== Tailwind ===
Use existing Tailwind conventions. IMPORTANT: Always use `search-docs` tool for version-specific Tailwind CSS documentation and updated code examples. Never rely on training data. IMPORTANT: Activate `tailwindcss-development` every time you're working with Tailwind CSS or styling-related tasks.

=== Fortify ===
Fortify is headless authentication with routes/controllers. IMPORTANT: Always use `search-docs` for detailed Laravel Fortify patterns/documentation. IMPORTANT: Activate `developing-with-fortify` for Fortify authentication features.
</laravel-boost-guidelines>
